item.title: A Global Euro Must First Win Over Europe
item.description: In a world of competing currency blocs, the euro is the dollar’s most credible rival. But for it to become a genuine counterweight to the greenback, the European Union must strengthen its financial foundations and expand its reach, starting with the member states that have not adopted it despite being obliged to do so.

item.title: Japan Needs Higher Interest Rates
item.description: In 2012, when Japan was dealing with chronic deflation, policymakers were right to embrace monetary easing, including lower interest rates. Today, however, Japan faces the opposite problem: a weak yen, combined with higher interest rates in the US, calls for a much tighter monetary policy.

item.title: A Middle-Powers Grand Strategy to Prevent Atrocities
item.description: Many governments have leverage to prevent atrocity crimes, yet lack the machinery to turn warnings into consistent, accountable action before it is too late. Now that three of the five permanent members of the Security Council are undercutting the postwar legal order, middle powers most close the gap.

item.title: Unleashing Africa’s Women Agripreneurs
item.description: Across Sub-Saharan Africa, women workers dominate agriculture but rarely capture the sector’s economic value. With a systematic approach to closing the gap, policymakers, NGOs, and philanthropic organizations could unlock a $1 trillion market and transform the continent’s food systems for the better.

item.title: Low Expectations for Israel’s Election
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel into a trap in which ever-increasing strategic commitments are outstripping the productive base that finances them, and the goodwill on which its alliances depend is being destroyed. While a new government would not transform Israeli foreign policy, it could begin to drag Israel out of its morass.

item.title: From AI Boom to Economic Bust
item.description: Contrary to tech optimists' rosy predictions, AI may prove to be a drag on growth. By concentrating wealth and economic opportunities in a few cities while destroying the low-cost jobs that have historically fueled global development, the technology could end up making much of the world poorer and more divided.

item.title: The Institutional Roots of Policy Nonsense
item.description: At a time when antimicrobial resistance threatens public health and our long-term economic well-being, tax policies favor financial engineering at the expense of developing new antibiotics. Similarly perverse incentives are at the heart of out-of-control public spending.

item.title: Is Christian Democracy Finished?
item.description: Traditionally, Christian Democrats believed that taking care of all groups in society could create a harmonious balance that would prevent instability and self-destructive infighting. But the conditions that enabled this strategy have changed, particularly in Germany, where Christian Democrats must reconnect with a different part of their history.

item.title: Independent AI Auditing Now
item.description: Recent hacking incidents confirm the need for independent scrutiny not only of what AI systems are capable of, but also of what their developers are doing to minimize harm and communicate honestly with the public. Even if AI auditing is still at an early stage, other industries have already provided a playbook.

item.title: Strict Liability for AI Executives
item.description: As an OpenAI whistleblower recently explained, AI executives have knowingly fostered a culture that “guarantees periodic failures,” the scale of which is “growing as systems get more capable.” This approach hinges on an expectation of impunity, which is why AI firms must be held legally accountable for the harm their agents cause.

item.title: Who Will Pay to Preserve Tropical Forests?
item.description: For decades, the international community has acknowledged the extraordinary value of tropical forests while failing to invest adequately in their conservation. The Tropical Forest Forever Facility, launched at last year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, could help close this financing gap.

item.title: Why Following in Milei’s Footsteps Would Be Bad for Brazil
item.description: Far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro holds up Argentine President Javier Milei’s economic program as a model for Brazil. But Milei's economic experiment has been a failure, leaving millions of Argentinians worse off and effectively turning their heavily indebted country into a client of the United States.

item.title: How Worried Should We Be About the Global Economy?
item.description: The risks to the global economy—including high inflation, soaring public debt, market concentration, and geopolitical volatility—are well known. But it is worth underscoring just how rare and dangerous it is for all of them to be salient at the same time.

item.title: How a Pause on Frontier AI Could Work
item.description: Whether the development of frontier AI should be paused is for policymakers to decide. But they should recognize that highly concentrated hardware supply chains make a pause feasible and, if implemented properly, likely to be sustainable.

item.title: Trump’s Latest Gift to Putin
item.description: Unable to win his foolish war against Iran, Donald Trump blames its consequences on Ukraine and uses the lie to justify ending sanctions against Russia, thereby extending that war as well. His diesel deal with the Kremlin is less about lowering gas prices for Americans and more about submitting to Vladimir Putin.

item.title: China’s Panda Diplomacy Is Losing Its Charm
item.description: Since giving a pair of giant pandas to the Smithsonian’s National Zoo in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s visit to Beijing, China has used panda loans as a means of projecting a harmless and friendly image globally. But it was always an act—and foreign audiences are no longer falling for it.

item.title: The Blindness of China’s All-Seeing State
item.description: China's relentless surveillance has taught people to perform obedience and loyalty, while keeping their beliefs hidden. This creates a dilemma for the ruling Communist Party: repression distorts the very information the government needs to understand society.

item.title: A Stronger Renminbi Is No Quick Fix for Global Imbalances
item.description: The near-consensus among financial commentators is that China's currency is undervalued, driving global imbalances. But the renminbi's weakness reflects weak domestic demand, and pursuing currency appreciation without addressing that issue head-on would be counterproductive for everyone.

item.title: Trump’s Misguided War Against Effective Altruism
item.description: The US Department of “War” has recently begun attacking effective altruism, a movement that aims to save lives, reduce suffering, and prevent future catastrophes. Why would the Trump administration, which with great fanfare created a Department of Government Efficiency, now oppose being effective?

item.title: Futureless Russia
item.description: During past periods of chaos and brutality in Russia, such as Stalin’s Great Terror, there was generally a sense that the country was headed somewhere—that the suffering served some end, however unjustifiable the means. But the repression Russians are enduring today has only one aim: to perpetuate the state that is executing it.
